summary: No confirmed verifier defect. Each SOP TM-07 rule has at least one hand-built golden case whose full report changes if that rule is missing or reversed, and the comparator matches the tolerance and exact-match promise in instruction.md. Batches that land exactly on a limit use binary-exact data, so a contract-valid alternative OLS or ordering formula cannot flip a flag or pass. Every assertion was traced statically; nothing was executed.
checks_performed: Checked that every file listed in packet-manifest.json was read in full. tests/shipped/tools/metalquant_run.py has the same hash as environment/app/tools/metalquant_run.py, so the verifier does not run a stale driver.

Traced compare() (tests/test_outputs.py:119-142) against instruction.md:7. The key sets, id/analyte/flag/ccv_ok/pass and null values are checked for exact type and value. value and recovery use rel 1e-6 when |e|>=1 and abs 1e-6 otherwise, which is the promised tolerance. Integer and float numbers are both accepted. blank_levels key order is ignored because the keys are compared as a set.

Recomputed the hand-built families by hand on the exact line (slope 10, intercept 100, response = counts/1024). Rechecked all rows of calibration, blank_mean, blank_nondetects, blank_single_result, blank_no_results, dilution, flag_basis, flag_limits, negative_readings, ccv_limits, ccv_bracketing, ccv_unbracketed, spike_recovery, spike_nondetects, section_one_limits and report_order. Every recomputed golden value agrees with the SOP rules and with the shipped-code fallback for values the SOP leaves undefined.

Checked each shipped defect against a case that rejects it. The through-origin fit (calib.py:14) fails calibration rows 1-4. The first-blank-only level (blanks.py:6-9) fails blank_mean rows 1-2 and blank_nondetects rows 1-3. The amount formula reading*dilution-level (samples.py:9) fails dilution W-72/W-73/W-74 and blank_mean W-32. Flagging on the amount (samples.py:13) fails flag_basis W-82/W-84 and section_one_limits HG-5S. The `<= loq` check fails flag_limits W-92 and HG-3. The strict unrounded CCV pass (qc.py:9) fails ccv_limits CCV-1/2/3/5/7. The previous-CCV-only bracket (qc.py:14-17) fails ccv_bracketing W-111. Dividing spike recovery by the dilution (qc.py:21) fails spike_recovery W-131S/W-133S.

Checked plausible wrong alternatives that are not the shipped bugs. Clamping negative readings to zero fails negative_readings W-103. Letting ND blanks into the mean fails blank_nondetects rows 1-3. A strict `> mdl` blank result test fails blank_nondetects row 2 (MB-10 reads exactly 1.0). Using the mean of all blank readings when there are no results fails blank_no_results rows 3-4. A fallback of 0.0 fails blank_no_results rows 2-4. Treating unbracketed runs as always true fails ccv_unbracketed row 2 (W-125). Using the nearest single CCV for unbracketed runs fails ccv_unbracketed row 4 (W-128). Using any earlier failed CCV instead of the nearest fails ccv_bracketing W-113. The SOP spike formula applied to ND pairs, or ND amounts set to 0, fails spike_nondetects W-141S/W-142S/W-141T/W-143S. Sorting runs or analytes fails report_order rows 1-2. Reporting the rounded CCV recovery fails ccv_limits CCV-3 (110.04 against a 1.1e-4 bound).

Checked float robustness at limit-landing cases. The standards and runs use is_counts 1024 and integer or dyadic responses, so centered, uncentered and statistics.linear_regression OLS all give the exact slope and intercept (10/100 for Pb, 976.5625/0 for Hg). The corrected readings 1.0, 5.0, 100 and 1000 are therefore exact. The just-off-limit cases (1e-8 relative, e.g. 0.99999995 and 4.99999995) sit far outside float noise. Section 1 guarantees CCV recoveries are never within 1e-6 of a rounding tie.

Checked the grading channel. The driver is replaced by the verifier copy after the delivered bytes are captured (test_outputs.py:52-63). The candidate package runs as nobody through the documented command with -I -S from a fresh cwd, and test.sh makes /app readable. No step relies on a candidate-controlled comparison or on candidate diagnostic output.

coverage_sweep.category: Map each required behavior to an assertion that fails if it is missing or reversed
coverage_sweep.reason: One test per SOP section, each comparing complete reports of hand-built batches (sections 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8). The shipped defect in every module is rejected by at least one named family, as listed in checks_performed.

coverage_sweep.category: Check the full core result, not just existence, keys or row count
coverage_sweep.reason: compare() checks exact top-level and per-entry key sets, list lengths and positional order, and every field value (numbers with tolerance, strings, booleans and null exactly) in all four sections.

coverage_sweep.category: Named domain rule has an isolating case, not only held-out variation
coverage_sweep.reason: Each named rule has its own hand-built family: fitted intercept, blanks anywhere, ND blanks excluded, single blank result, no blank results, blank before dilution, flag basis, exact mdl/loq, negative readings, rounded inclusive CCV, two-sided bracketing, unbracketed fallback, spike recovery of results, ND spike fallback, section 1 extremes, and report order. The generated and capacity batches add variation on top of these.

Traced the shipped code and at least ten plausible alternative mistakes (clamping, strict limits, fallback 0.0, fallback to the mean of readings, nearest-single-CCV, any-earlier-CCV, SOP spike formula on ND pairs, sorting, rounded recovery). Each changes at least one compared field in a named fixture.

coverage_sweep.category: Contract-valid alternatives (formatting, ordering, implementation) are accepted
coverage_sweep.reason: blank_levels key order is ignored, int and float are both accepted, and JSON whitespace is irrelevant because the output is parsed. Numeric tolerance matches the instruction. At the exact-limit and CCV-rounding boundaries the data is binary-exact or kept away from ties, so different valid OLS formulas, operation orders or rounding methods give the same flags and passes.

coverage_sweep.category: Documented restrictions and lifecycle (unchanged driver, documented command)
coverage_sweep.reason: The delivered driver bytes are compared to the shipped copy. Batches run through the verifier-owned driver at the documented path against the candidate's /app/src. No undocumented restriction is imposed beyond the SOP report shape.

coverage_sweep.category: State machine initialization-to-first-event (CCV bracketing before first / after last / none)
coverage_sweep.reason: Samples before the first CCV (true, even when that CCV fails: W-128), after a last CCV that passes (W-123) or fails (W-125), and batches with no CCV (row 3) are all graded against the shipped-check fallback.

coverage_sweep.category: Signed derived quantities discriminated across sign partitions
coverage_sweep.reason: Negative readings, a negative blank level (-1.0 through the fallback), a negative corrected reading, and negative spike recoveries (-150, -15, -16.04) are graded as exact expected numbers. None of them is accepted through an approximate-zero check.

coverage_sweep.category: Proxy behavior, stale binaries, self-controlled comparisons, unreachable cases
coverage_sweep.reason: The goldens are sealed and pinned by sha256 in ROSTER. The driver copy is identical to the delivered one. The candidate supplies only stdout JSON, which is compared to verifier-owned expectations. Every fixture batch stays within the SOP section 1 limits (spot-checked the mdl/loq, dilution, is_counts and CCV true>=10*loq constraints in the hand-built and generated rows).

coverage_sweep.category: Native encoding / representation vs semantic content
coverage_sweep.reason: The verifier parses JSON and compares values. It does not compare bytes, key order within entries, or whitespace. The exact list order it requires is promised by SOP section 8 and instruction.md.

rules: Blank level is the mean of blank results (section 4)
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: blank_nondetects row 2: MB-10 reads exactly 1.0 = mdl and is included; MB-11 at 0.75 is excluded; level 2.0. Row 3: MB-37 at 0.99999995 is excluded; level 3.0.

rules: Blank level with no results falls back to the shipped calculation
Readings may be below nought and the blank is subtracted before dilution
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: negative_readings: the level is -1.0 from the ND blank, W-103 reads 0.0, is corrected to 1.0 and gets J with value 2.0. A clamped or 0.0-fallback implementation gives ND.

rules: Flags judged on the corrected reading (section 5)
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: flag_basis W-82: corrected 3 gives J while the amount is 12 (>loq). HG-5S: corrected 900 gives J while the amount is 1800 (>loq 1000). Both reject flag-on-amount.

rules: Non-detect parent or spike keeps the shipped calculation on SOP amounts
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: spike_nondetects W-141S (parent ND) gives 48.75 through the shipped formula with dilution; the SOP formula would give 97.5. spike_recovery W-133S (both results, blank 2.0, dilutions 4 and 8) gives 380 with no dilution divisor.

rules: CCV pass on the recovery rounded to one decimal, inclusive (section 6)
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: ccv_limits CCV-3 (110.04) passes but must be reported as 110.04. CCV-2 (110.00000000000001) passes. CCV-4 (110.06) and CCV-6 (89.94) fail.

rules: Bracketing by the nearest CCV on each side is per analyte
Report order follows run order and then analyte order
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: report_order row 1: A-CCV fails for Tl and Pb only, so ccv_ok is false for those analytes and true for As/Cd on Z-9 and B-SPK. The analytes are listed non-alphabetically.
section_one_limits HG-1 reads exactly 100 (J) and HG-3 reads exactly 1000 (empty flag, value 1e6). The line is binary-exact, so a valid formula variant cannot flip these flags.
